title: "rush sql"

```{term}
#| include: false
rush run -o mtcars.csv 'mtcars'
```

The `sql` command runs a [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) query directly against
your files, with no import step. Each file becomes a relation named after the
file, so you can reference it right in the query.

## Usage

```bash
rush sql [options] [<query>] [--] [<file>...]
```

## Basic queries

Run a SQL query against one or more files:

```{term}
rush sql "SELECT mpg, cyl, hp, wt FROM mtcars WHERE hp > 200 ORDER BY hp DESC" mtcars.csv
```

## Aggregations

DuckDB's full SQL is available, including aggregations, window functions, and CTEs:

```{term}
rush sql "SELECT cyl,
                 COUNT(*) AS n,
                 ROUND(AVG(mpg), 1) AS avg_mpg,
                 MIN(hp) AS min_hp,
                 MAX(hp) AS max_hp
          FROM mtcars
          GROUP BY cyl
          ORDER BY cyl" mtcars.csv
```

## Querying Parquet files

Parquet files are registered via DuckDB's `read_parquet`, so large-file queries
run without loading everything into memory:

```{term}
rush convert -o mtcars.parquet mtcars.csv
rush sql "SELECT cyl, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(mpg), 1) AS avg_mpg
          FROM mtcars
          GROUP BY cyl
          ORDER BY avg_mpg DESC" mtcars.parquet
```

## Querying DuckDB databases

A `.duckdb` file is attached as a schema, and its tables are accessible as
`schema.table`:

```{term}
rush convert -o mtcars.duckdb mtcars.csv
rush sql "SELECT m.mpg, m.hp, m.wt
          FROM mtcars.mtcars m
          WHERE m.hp > 200
          ORDER BY m.hp DESC" mtcars.duckdb
```

## Querying standard input

Use `-` to read CSV from stdin as a relation named `stdin`:

```{term}
echo "item,price,qty
apple,1.20,10
banana,0.80,25
cherry,3.50,5" | rush sql "SELECT item, price * qty AS total FROM stdin ORDER BY total DESC" -
```

## Joining multiple files

Pass multiple files and each becomes a relation you can join:

```{term}
echo "cyl,engine_type
4,inline
6,v-type
8,v-type" > engines.csv
rush sql "SELECT m.mpg, m.hp, m.cyl, e.engine_type
          FROM mtcars m JOIN engines e ON m.cyl = e.cyl
          WHERE m.hp > 150
          ORDER BY m.hp DESC" mtcars.csv engines.csv
```

## Saving SQL results

Pipe a SQL result to Parquet or another file:

```{term}
rush sql -o powerful.parquet "SELECT * FROM mtcars WHERE hp > 150" mtcars.csv
rush run 'nrow(df)' powerful.parquet
```

## Piping with SQL

The result of a query is an ordinary data frame, so everything composes:

```{term}
rush run 'head(df, 10)' mtcars.csv | rush sql "SELECT cyl, COUNT(*) AS n FROM stdin GROUP BY cyl" -
```

## Dry run

See the generated script that runs the query:

```{term}
rush sql -n "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mtcars" mtcars.csv
```

## Help

```{term}
rush sql -h
```

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f mtcars.csv mtcars.parquet mtcars.duckdb engines.csv powerful.parquet
```
